name: H.264 Delivery Ladder

measured.ladder: Derived from ~60 measured encodes across three venues, two codecs and six heights, VMAF proven both ways, two human observers. 540p, 480p and 240p were REMOVED: measured against a 1080p screen they are dominated at every file size by the rung above. They are not cheaper options, they are worse options that happen to be smaller.
measured.rates: 1080p 5.0 Mbps scores 91.7 on the hardest clip in the library at 48-51% of the master's size. 720p 2.75 Mbps scores 92.6 on a 720p screen. 360p 600 kbps scores 86.9 on a 360p screen - the emergency rung was never dominated, it was previously configured at a size where it had no business competing.
measured.full_length_baseline: Run 40, 2026-08-23, MONDAY DOGS REG AND NONREG BTCA2026, 99.3 min. Under the OLD crf-targeted presets the 720p rung produced 4.23 Mbps at 77% of its 5500k ceiling - not the 2.9-3.4 Mbps the previous clip-derived note predicted. Ceilings DO shape a full-length encode. This is why the ladder is now rate-targeted.

rate_control: TARGET RATE. rate_kbps is the average bitrate; maxrate and bufsize bound the peak. crf remains as a fallback for any rung without a rate_kbps.

rules.never_upscale: Skip any rung STRICTLY ABOVE source height. Report SKIPPED (blue), not FAILED (red).
rules.master_is_never_a_deliverable: RULED 2026-08-23. The master is an encoding source and an archive, never a customer download. Every file a customer receives is produced here. The former master_is_top_rung skip is retired.
rules.aspect: Scale by height with -2 width. Preserve source aspect. No padding.
rules.top_rung_is_derived: The 1080p rate is reduced per film so the file stays under 4 GiB, capped at 5000 and REFUSED below 3500 kbps - past 148.6 minutes, where 720p and the HEVC rung carry the film. [MEASURED 2026-08-25 against the live constants.] This threshold MOVES with the reserve: it was 152 min at a 3% reserve and is 148.6 at 5%. Recompute it rather than quoting this number after any change.
rules.rejected_2pass: 2-pass VBR rejected at THIS stage 2026-08-23: the production master is itself 2-pass from autumn 2026, so the bit reallocation has already happened upstream. Doubling encode time to repeat it is paying twice for one insight.
